about: Team notes (platform.memory, scope business, class practice) and the proposals that made or tried to make them (platform.proposal). Every team note is published by an approved proposal. 'visible_from' is the note's min_rank at T; 'lowered' says a senior lowered it from the proposer's rank. 'review' is the 90-day check (tenant setting): kept, or still waiting at T (state unverified).

team_notes.subject: Uncollected cars
team_notes.text: Storage is charged from day three after the car is ready.
team_notes.why: Finished cars left on the lot take the parking Charlotte Pike needs for the next day's work.
team_notes.how: When a customer asks about leaving a finished car, or a draft mentions storage.
team_notes.fixed_by: kb/CROSS-STORE.md 1.1, ledger kb.team_note.storage; contradicts policies/storage-of-uncollected-cars.md on purpose

team_notes.subject: Discount approval
team_notes.text: A discount above 10 % needs the shop senior's approval, recorded on the order
team_notes.why: Unapproved discounts on cash orders at Charlotte Pike went unnoticed for six months.
team_notes.how: Before an answer, an estimate or a draft offers or records a discount above 10 % of the bill before tax.

team_notes.subject: First call
team_notes.text: On a first call, offer a time before the price
team_notes.why: Calls where a time came first ended in a booking more often.
team_notes.how: Drafts and coaching for a new enquiry, by phone or chat.

team_notes.subject: Shop names
team_notes.text: Call the shops East Main, Bonny Oaks and Charlotte Pike; never main, east or west
team_notes.why: The short keys belong to the system; nobody in the company says them.
team_notes.how: Every answer and draft that names a shop.

team_notes.subject: Money in answers
team_notes.text: Say whether an amount is before or after sales tax, every time
team_notes.why: The office and the counter were quoting the same bill two ways.
team_notes.how: Any amount in an answer to staff.

team_notes.subject: Missed callers
team_notes.text: A missed caller is called back within the hour; claim the call before you dial
team_notes.why: Two advisors rang the same caller back on one morning, and a third caller got nobody.
team_notes.how: Lists and drafts about call backs.

team_notes.subject: Parts promises
team_notes.text: Promise a pickup day only after the parts manager confirms the delivery
team_notes.why: Promised days were missed when a part came a day late.
team_notes.how: Answers and drafts that give a customer a ready date.

team_notes.subject: Times across shops
team_notes.text: Charlotte Pike runs on Central time; name the zone whenever a time crosses shops
team_notes.why: Two bookings and a parts delivery were read an hour off.
team_notes.how: Any time shown to people in both cities.

team_notes.subject: Desks, not people
team_notes.text: Compare missed calls by desk and by shop; never rank advisors on them
team_notes.why: A missed call rings a desk and has no person.
team_notes.how: Any comparison of phone work that includes missed calls.

team_notes.subject: Customer drafts
team_notes.text: Drafts to customers: no emoji, no 'unfortunately', one clear next step at the end
team_notes.why: Customers answered the drafts that ended in a time or a question.
team_notes.how: Every draft to a customer, on any channel.

team_notes.subject: Old parts
team_notes.text: On brake and suspension jobs, offer the old parts back at pickup
team_notes.why: Seeing the worn part settles most doubts about the bill.
team_notes.how: Pickup messages and drafts for those jobs.

team_notes.subject: Shift changes
team_notes.text: A shift change is asked for in the app; the answer comes by Thursday noon
team_notes.why: Swaps agreed in the hallway left the roster wrong twice in one month.
team_notes.how: When anyone asks to change the hours or the day of a shift, or to drop one.

team_notes.subject: Comebacks
team_notes.text: Call a job a comeback only when its order is tied to the first one; otherwise say repeat visit
team_notes.why: Comeback counts mixed warranty returns with customers coming back for new work.
team_notes.how: Any count, list or draft about returned work.

team_notes.subject: Declined work
team_notes.text: When a customer declines work, write the reason on the order in one line
team_notes.why: The next advisor starts from that line.
team_notes.how: Notes and drafts after an estimate is declined.

proposals.subject: Booking read-back
proposals.text: Read the booking back before hanging up
proposals.why: Customers came on the wrong day after a call that ended without a summary.
proposals.how: Coaching and call summaries for booked visits.
proposals.reason: the page 'Booking a visit' already says this; propose the wording there

proposals.subject: Phone greeting
proposals.text: Answer the phone with the shop's name and your own name
proposals.why: Callers ask who they are talking to, and a name on the call starts it better.
proposals.how: Coaching and call summaries at every shop.
proposals.reason: Folks here know who they called. Not needed.

source.said: I'd like to propose one for everybody: answer with the shop's name and your own name.

proposals.subject: Photo first
proposals.text: Show the worn part or a photo before naming a price
proposals.why: A customer who has seen the part rarely argues the price.
proposals.how: Drafts and coaching about found work.
proposals.reason: Withdrawn by the person who proposed it.

source.said: Propose this for the team, please: show the worn part or a photo before you name a price.

proposals.subject: Company drivers
proposals.text: A company driver cannot approve work over 300 USD; call the fleet contact
proposals.why: A driver said 'go ahead' to work above the limit and nobody had told her there was one.
proposals.how: When work is found on a company account's vehicle and only the driver is there.

proposals.subject: Prices source
proposals.text: Take prices from the price list page, never from a service page
proposals.how: Whenever a price is quoted or drafted.
